content.text: {"conditions":{"rc1":{"status":"review","note":"The path from the articulated reasons (Proctor's mistaken belief, full testing time confirmed by the consultant, Merit Promotion Score of 64.4 below cut-offs, selectee qualifications and rankings) to the no-discrimination conclusion is largely traceable, but the record never states Complainant's protected bases (only implying race via White and Hispanic comparators, plus reprisal) and does not analyze whether the conceded proctoring errors affected his score."},"rc2":{"status":"review","note":"Most characterizations are attributed to named roles (Proctor, Chief DUSM, Assistant Chief, Branch Chief, Career Board Presenter, testing consultant), but some are unattributed (that the Proctor was 'trained and certified,' that 'two more qualified candidates were selected,' that he did not apply for two of 13 vacancies), and conflicting accounts are left unreconciled (the Proctor patting down all candidates versus two others; no prohibited items versus a cell phone found)."},"rc3":{"status":"review","note":"Key dates are given (August 31, 2017 exam; September 11, 2017 meeting; November 2, 2017 selections; June 2019 decision withdrawn; June 2021 re-issued), but the procedural history appears out of sequence and the dates of Complainant's EEO contact and of the prior pat-downs ('a week before') are not fixed, which matters for the reprisal-knowledge timeline."},"rc4":{"status":"review","note":"The legal framework is stated (legitimate nondiscriminatory reasons, pretext, preponderance) and Complainant's assertions and admissions are addressed, but the official who issued the final decision and the actual selecting official for each vacancy (as opposed to the Career Board Presenter and Assistant Chief who explained the selections) are not identified."},"rc5":{"status":"review","note":"The record contains substantial testimony and score data from which an independent reviewer could evaluate much of the decision, but the unstated protected bases, unreconciled factual conflicts, and missing dates and decision-maker identities mean outside context would be needed to fully assess support for the conclusion."}}}
